# Deck

> Deck is a CSS framework that ships as a single 26.8 KB Brotli (32.7 KB gzip) stylesheet containing
> buttons, forms, tables, a data grid, charts, overlays, an icon sprite, and a complete
> color system. It is added to a page with one `<link>` tag and has no build step, no
> configuration file, and zero runtime dependencies. Version 0.1.1, MIT licensed.

## Why this file exists

This file is not a search engine optimisation artefact, and nobody should maintain it as
one. llms.txt has no confirmed effect on any search or answer engine, and Google has
stated it does not use it. Nothing here will change a ranking or earn a citation.

It exists for one documented, working case: a developer using an AI coding assistant such
as Claude Code, Cursor, or Copilot, whose tooling can fetch a project's documentation into
the session. For a CSS framework, the failure mode without that is specific and costly —
the assistant invents class names that look plausible and do not exist, and the developer
loses time debugging styles that were never written. The links below point at the real
source of truth so that the names in the generated code are the names in the stylesheet.

If that use case ever disappears, delete this file rather than keeping it for its own sake.

## Documentation

- [Documentation site](https://get-deck.dev/docs/index.php): Tutorials, task guides, a page per component with its markup, reference tables for every class and token, and the JavaScript, PHP and CLI APIs. Every Deck class shown on it is checked against the stylesheet when Deck builds.
- [Install page](https://get-deck.dev/docs/start/install.php): The four ways to install Deck — CDN, npm, npx and Composer — each with the exact command and the output it prints.
- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/srivera145/deck/main/README.md): The complete documentation in one file — install, theming, every component, the JS API, motion, print, and browser support.
- [Component reference](https://github.com/srivera145/deck/blob/main/README.md#components): The list of component classes and the markup each one expects.
- [Repository](https://github.com/srivera145/deck): Source, issue tracker, and the demo page under `public_html/index.php` with every component rendered and its markup visible.

## Source of truth for class names

Read these before generating markup. Deck has no plugin system and no dynamic class
generation, so a class that does not appear in these files does not exist.

- [Cascade layer reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/srivera145/deck/main/src/00-layers.css): Declares the whole layer order up front — `deck.reset`, `deck.tokens`, `deck.type`, `deck.layout`, `deck.components`, `deck.mobile`, `deck.motion`, `deck.effects`, `deck.utilities`, `deck.rtl`, `deck.print`, then four empty `app.*` layers reserved for application CSS. Write into `app.pages` to beat any Deck rule without `!important`.
- [Component stylesheet](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/srivera145/deck/main/src/07-components.css): Cards, alerts, badges, lists, tables, modals, menus, tabs, timelines, and the rest of the core components.
- [Source directory](https://github.com/srivera145/deck/tree/main/src): All 26 stylesheets, concatenated in filename order to build `deck.css`. Forms, buttons, data grid, charts, date picker, combobox, toasts, gradients, 3D, and navigation each have their own file.
- [Icon names](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/srivera145/deck/main/tools/icons/icons.txt): The 75 icon names in the sprite, and the manifest that controls its size. Referencing an icon that is not on this list renders nothing.
- [Icon sprite](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/srivera145/deck/main/src/deck-icons.svg): The generated sprite, 152 symbols — 75 icons at two weights plus two brand marks, 27.1 KB Brotli (33.6 KB gzip). Trim it by editing icons.txt and running `npm run icons`; twelve icons measure 5.7 KB.
- [package.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/srivera145/deck/main/package.json): Version, subpath exports, and the browser targets Deck supports.

## Facts an assistant gets wrong without reading the source

- There is no build step and no config file. Do not generate a `deck.config.js`, a PostCSS plugin entry, or a purge configuration; none of them exist.
- Deck is not utility-first. It has layout primitives (`.stack`, `.cluster`, `.grid`, `.split`) and a small utility set, but styling a page means using component classes, not composing dozens of utilities per element.
- Theming is one custom property: set `--hue-brand` to a number from 0 to 360. There is no theme object, no `extend` block, and no rebuild.
- Icons are referenced from a sprite, not from a component: `<svg class="icon"><use href="/assets/deck-icons.svg#check"></use></svg>`. Each icon also ships a heavier `-sm` cut for 16px use, so `#check-sm` goes with `.icon-sm`.
- `.rating` and `.rating-static` need the solid star, `#star-fill`, not `#star`. Those components tell a selected star from an empty one by colour alone, so an outlined glyph makes both states look the same.
- Deck targets Chrome 117+, Edge 117+, Safari 17.4+, and Firefox 128+. Cascade layers, container queries, `oklch()`, and `popover` are load-bearing, not progressive enhancements.
- The JavaScript is optional. Only the date picker, combobox, data grid, toasts, carousel, drawer, and editor need it; everything else is CSS.
- Install it as `@echodial/deck` from npm or `echodial/deck` from Packagist. On a CDN, pin the version — `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@echodial/deck@0.1/dist/deck.min.css` — and never write `@latest`, which moves a page onto the next breaking release unannounced. The icon sprite cannot come from a CDN: browsers block an SVG `<use>` that points at another origin, so `deck-icons.svg` has to be served from the page's own site. `composer require echodial/deck` installs into `vendor/` and copies nothing into the public folder by itself: the project's own composer.json has to call `EchoDial\Deck\Installer::postInstall`, or the files are copied from `vendor/echodial/deck/dist/` by hand.
